title: Can the changes in subcutaneous fat tissue in patients with lipedema, lipohypertrophy, and lymphedema be distinguished by technical diagnostic examinations?
summary:
The diagnosis of lipedema was described in the 1950s, but was then forgotten for many decades and has only come back into focus since 2000. There were many descriptions and hardly any studies on it; this has slowly changed, including the differentiation between lipedema (with pain on palpation), lipohypertrophy (without pain), and lymphedema. Well-trained physicians can make this distinction clinically, but for physicians outside the specialty, or physicians without experience, it is helpful for diagnosis if there are measuring devices that can confirm the diagnoses. In addition, we need reliable measuring devices for studies on the treatment of these conditions, to be sure whether treatment can measurably change the severity of the disease — in other words, with devices that can assess the extent of the condition.
In this study, no “new” measuring devices or medical products will be used; however, devices that are commonly used in other fields will be applied, and their diagnostic value for distinguishing the conditions lipedema, lipohypertrophy, and lymphedema will be compared. The aim is to find out whether there is a device that can identify these diseases particularly well and could also demonstrate improvement in the clinical picture.
The following examinations / questionnaires will be used for all participants (irrespective of the study group) and will take approximately 90 minutes:
• Quality-of-life questionnaire regarding pain in venous and lymphatic diseases
• Bodytronic 600 by the company Bauerfeind (contact-free measuring device for leg circumferences)
• the ultrasound device of the vein practice (GE Logic Book)
• the elastometer ultrasound device: MarvoS 80 Elite Ultrasound System from SonoScape
• the LymphScanner (company Delfin)
• the SkinFibroMeter (company Delfin)
• the application of a blood pressure cuff on the thigh and the calf
The examination procedure is as follows:
• Completing a questionnaire regarding impairments caused by lymphedema and lipedema
• Measurement of height and weight
• Measurement of waist circumference (Waist-to-Height Ratio)
• Circumference measurement of the legs using the “Bodytronic” device from Bauerfeind: this is a measuring device in which you stand on a platform that rotates around itself in 50 seconds and electronically records your leg circumferences using light and reflection
• Circumference measurement at the ankle, below the knee, and at the thigh by hand (measuring tape)
• Photographic documentation of the legs in front of a white wall from front and back, as well as from both sides
• The following measurements are performed in the groin, on the inner and outer thigh, on the inner calf, and on the forearm, both on the right and left side:
o Examination by hand for pain on pressure in the adipose tissue and in the muscle tissue
o Ultrasound of the skin and the subcutaneous adipose tissue up to the muscle fascia to measure the thickness of the individual layers and to determine whether fluid is visible on ultrasound
o Ultrasound of the same region with the elastometer (works like an ultrasound device)
o Measurement of the proportion of connective tissue (Delfin Fibrometer) and water (Delfin Moisturemeter) (works similarly to an ultrasound device) in the previously described areas
• Afterwards, a blood pressure cuff is placed on the thigh and the calf while lying down and slowly inflated. As soon as you notice pain, you say so; this pressure value will be recorded and the inflation will be stopped, and the pressure released.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women between 18 and 70 years of age with a clinically confirmed diagnosis (Group I: lipedema, Group II: lipohypertrophy, Group III: lymphedema) or exclusion of these diagnoses (control group, Group IV).
Exclusion criteria:
• Saphenous vein insufficiency (excluded by investigator beforehand by ultrasound)
• Diabetic neuropathy
• Use of edema-inducing antihypertensive medication (in particular amlodipine and ramipril)
• Pregnancy (not due to any risk to the pregnant woman or the unborn child, but due to the possible influence on edema formation)
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Insufficient ability to communicate in German
• Participation in other studies within the last 4 weeks.
